instrument.state: A dynamic system accepts a controlled change in an input and exposes an output whose evolution through time can be observed.
instrument.operation: Apply a known step change to the input and record the output trajectory from its initial state through the transient response toward its later behavior.
instrument.signal: The output trajectory exhibits measurable temporal features such as delay, rise, overshoot, oscillation, peak, settling, and steady-state change.
instrument.inference: Those response features constrain empirical properties of the system's dynamics and can distinguish candidate models or characterize how the system reacts to perturbation.
instrument.limit: Noise, unknown initial state, saturation, nonlinear behavior, disturbances, interacting inputs, insufficient observation time, and dependence on the chosen operating point can distort the response or make conclusions fail to generalize beyond the tested perturbation.

target.question: Which bounded changes measurably reduce delay in process P-17 under the tested operating point?

mapping.state: Process P-17 runs at the stated operating point. The tested input is a bounded increase in its intake-priority setting. The operator can apply, hold and reverse the setting while recording a time series. All stated execution conditions are satisfied.
mapping.operation: Apply the priority step, hold it for the observation window, reverse it and repeat. Keep staffing and arrival schedule fixed. Record the output trajectory through the transient and the later window, and retain the step and reversal timestamps.
mapping.signal: The archived trajectory is the smoothed submitted-priority register in command units. In each of three repetitions it settles two units below its initial value after the step and returns after reversal. The acquisition filter generates the transient from the submitted command before the work-item scheduler acts.
mapping.inference:
The repeated response establishes a two-hour reduction in end-to-end delay from the tested intake-priority change in P-17 at this operating point.
The recorded timestamps and register values permit a plot of the submitted priority trajectory through the step and reversal windows of P-17.
mapping.limit: The register records submitted input, not queue state, completion times or application to work items. No process-output channel or conversion from command units to delay is supplied. Execution of the stated input operation is already granted; the filter is part of the recorder, not P-17 processing.
